name: Lambda
founded: 2012 (GPU cloud from 2018; on-prem hardware exited August 2025)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Lambda is the developer-DNA neocloud converting itself into a contracted 'Superintelligence Cloud' ahead of a reported H2 2026 IPO — a multibillion-dollar multi-year Microsoft deployment agreement (November 2025), NVIDIA as simultaneous supplier, Series D investor, and reportedly largest customer (a $1.5B four-year leaseback of ~18,000 of its own GPUs, per The Information), a >$1.5B Series E at $5.9B post-money (Forge round data; Lambda never disclosed the valuation), and the first investment-grade-rated Term Loan B by a private neocloud ($926M, Baa2, SOFR+300bps, August 2026). BACKGROUND: Founded 2012 in San Francisco by Stephen and Michael Balaban; sold GPU workstations and servers for a decade before going cloud-only (hardware exited August 2025; Inference API and Lambda Chat sunset September 2025). Michel Combes (ex-Sprint, Alcatel-Lucent, SoftBank International) replaced founder Stephen Balaban as CEO in May 2026; stated target is 3 GW of AI compute under management by 2030 against a footprint whose largest disclosed site is ~100 MW potential. SemiAnalysis ClusterMAX holds Lambda at Silver — two tiers below CoreWeave's Platinum — across both rating cycles.
ecosystemRole: We assess Lambda as the price-and-flexibility neocloud moving up-market into the CoreWeave model — and as a demand signal rather than a power buyer for most of this ecosystem's vendors, because its footprint is colocation-first (EdgeConneX Chicago, Cologix Columbus, Prime Data Centers Vernon, Aligned DFW) with owned 'AI factories' only now emerging (Kansas City, 24 MW scaling to 100 MW+). Basis: company site-level disclosures and trade press; no company-wide MW or GPU-fleet figure has ever been published — a collection gap its S-1 would close. For power-chain vendors the read-through is indirect: Lambda's 600 kW-rack Chicago build and hydrogen-powered GB300 deployment at ECL Mountain View show where high-density neocloud requirements are heading, but the facility capex mostly belongs to its colocation landlords.

productsAndServices.name: On-demand GPU cloud (Instances, Workspaces, Bare Metal)
productsAndServices.description: Self-serve NVIDIA instances billed by the minute with no egress fees: B200 SXM6 at $6.69–6.99/GPU-hr, H100 SXM at $3.99–4.29, GH200 at $2.29, down to V100 at $0.79 (published pricing, August 2026). Bare Metal Instances (May 2026) remove the hypervisor entirely — lifecycle managed through NVIDIA BlueField DPUs in zero-trust mode, first on GB300 NVL72. Workspaces (June 2026) added free multi-region organization/access-control containers.
highlights: Per-minute billing, no egress fees, no waitlist positioning
B200 on-demand launched August 2025 'no waitlists or commitments'
Pre-installed Lambda Stack (PyTorch/CUDA) — the developer-first heritage
productsAndServices.positioning: The price leader among major neoclouds — Sacra put Lambda's H100 PCIe at $2.49/GPU-hr vs CoreWeave's $4.25; ClusterMAX calls it a 'top-tier on-demand provider' even while holding the company at Silver overall.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Self-serve dashboard/API; contact-sales only for reserved terms beyond one year.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Vera Rubin NVL72 instances at general availability of the platform (H2 2026).

productsAndServices.name: 1-Click Clusters
productsAndServices.description: Self-serve multi-node clusters from 16 to 2,000+ GPUs (HGX B200 or H100) on Quantum-2 InfiniBand with NVIDIA SHARP in-network aggregation, managed Kubernetes or Slurm, terms from two weeks to a year. Published pricing: B200 at $8.87–9.86/GPU-hr by tier, H100 at $5.54–6.16.
highlights: 16-GPU evaluation clusters bookable for two weeks — no negotiation
SHARP enabled July 2025; FP4 workflows promoted on B200
productsAndServices.positioning: The mid-scale flexibility wedge: Sacra highlights Lambda partitioning 16,000+-GPU clusters into small allocations rentable in 15-minute increments, against CoreWeave's multi-year committed model.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Self-serve with published prices; reserved 1-year+ via sales.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Blackwell-Ultra 1CC on Quantum-X800 InfiniBand (6.4 Tb/s, rail-optimized) announced.

productsAndServices.name: Superclusters (single-tenant contracted capacity)
productsAndServices.description: Single-tenant, shared-nothing deployments from 4,000 to 165,000+ GPUs built on GB300 NVL72, HGX B300, and (H2 2026) Vera Rubin NVL72 rack systems, with managed Kubernetes/Slurm under SLA and co-engineering. This is the layer the Microsoft agreement (November 2025, tens of thousands of GPUs including GB300 NVL72) and the NVIDIA leaseback run through.
highlights: MLPerf Training v6.0 (June 2026): fastest GB300 NVL72 submission — Llama 3.1 8B in 11.59 min, ahead of NVIDIA's own entry
GB300 NVL72 live on Lambda Cloud October 2025
Industry-first hydrogen-powered GB300 NVL72 systems online at ECL Mountain View (September 2025)
productsAndServices.positioning: Converts Lambda from developer cloud into a CoreWeave-style contracted operator; ClusterMAX 2.0 (November 2025) still rates Lambda Silver vs CoreWeave Platinum and Nebius/Crusoe/Fluidstack Gold, citing capacity sell-outs, immature Kubernetes, and weak inference support.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Multi-year committed contracts; private cloud and dedicated bare-metal variants.
targetSegments: Frontier labs, quant finance (Hudson River Trading, May 2026)
productsAndServices.roadmap: 3 GW of AI compute under management and 1M+ GPUs targeted by 2030 (company statements).

productsAndServices.name: AI factories (data-center layer)
productsAndServices.description: Lambda's physical footprint: 'contiguous AI factories' (75 MW+ campuses) and 'distributed AI factories' (5–75 MW metro sites), overwhelmingly leased from colocation partners today — EdgeConneX Chicago (23 MW, 600+ kW racks, RFS 2026) and Atlanta, Cologix Columbus (HGX B200, 44 kW air-cooled racks), Prime Data Centers Vernon CA (21 of 33 MW), Aligned DFW-04 Plano — plus the first owned-scale conversion in Kansas City, MO (~$500M, 24 MW at early-2026 launch, >10,000 Blackwell Ultra GPUs, scalable past 100 MW, dedicated to a single unnamed customer).
highlights: Hydrogen fuel-cell off-grid GB300 site with ECL: zero-emissions, water byproduct recycled into liquid cooling
Joined Open Compute Project January 2026; early bet on co-packaged optics
productsAndServices.positioning: Colocation-heavy against Crusoe's energy-first owned campuses and CoreWeave's 1 GW+ active power — no operating Lambda site above ~100 MW potential has been documented; the gigawatt language is forward-looking.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Capacity delivered through Lambda's cloud contracts; facilities leased or (Kansas City) owned.
targetSegments: Its own cloud customers — the data-center layer is not sold standalone
productsAndServices.roadmap: 1 MW rack-scale designs on the AI-infrastructure roadmap; 2 GW+ vision with 1M+ GPUs by end of decade (EdgeConneX release).

recentDevelopments.headline: Priced $926M senior secured Term Loan B — Baa2 (Moody's), 'first investment-grade-rated TLB by a private neocloud'; SOFR+300bps (tightened 75bps from initial ~+375 talk on a ~$917M launch per Bloomberg), fully amortizing to Dec 2030, collateralized by GPU servers and contracted cash flows for an investment-grade offtaker
recentDevelopments.read: The debt market now prices Lambda's contracted cash flows like CoreWeave's — GPU-collateralized lending has matured from 15%-coupon exotica to investment grade in ~2 years, and the loan is explicitly tied to an NVIDIA-linked chip purchase.

recentDevelopments.headline: Hudson River Trading multi-year cloud agreement — Lambda becomes the quant firm's third compute provider
recentDevelopments.read: First marquee non-tech-platform win of 2026; diversification evidence for the pre-IPO narrative, though value and GPU counts were not disclosed.

recentDevelopments.headline: Closed $1B senior secured credit facility (J.P. Morgan lead, oversubscribed) — upsized ~4x from the $275M facility established August 2025
recentDevelopments.read: The debt ladder keeps pace with contracted demand; proceeds fund next-generation NVIDIA fleet and data-center capacity.

recentDevelopments.headline: Michel Combes (ex-Sprint/Alcatel-Lucent/SoftBank International CEO) appointed CEO; founder Stephen Balaban moves to CTO, Michael Balaban to CPO; John Donovan (ex-AT&T Communications CEO) becomes chairman
recentDevelopments.read: A telecom-infrastructure operator installed for gigawatt-scale capex and public markets — the clearest pre-IPO professionalization signal a private company can send.

recentDevelopments.headline: Vera Rubin NVL72 announced as core Supercluster building block; production availability H2 2026
recentDevelopments.read: First-wave access to NVIDIA's next rack generation keeps Lambda in the same silicon cadence as CoreWeave and Nebius.

recentDevelopments.headline: Reported: ≥$350M Mubadala-led pre-IPO convertible priced ~20% below eventual IPO price, with extra equity/cash owed if no listing within a year; IPO timing slips from H1 to H2 2026 (The Information)
recentDevelopments.read: A contractual forcing mechanism on the IPO clock — every quarter of delay now has an explicit cost.

recentDevelopments.headline: Series E of over $1.5B led by TWG Global with US Innovative Technology Fund — $5.9B post-money per Forge round data (valuation never company-disclosed)
recentDevelopments.read: Raised two weeks after the Microsoft agreement; the equity market paid up for contracted-backlog conversion, not the developer cloud.

recentDevelopments.headline: Multibillion-dollar multi-year Microsoft agreement: Lambda deploys AI infrastructure with tens of thousands of NVIDIA GPUs including GB300 NVL72
recentDevelopments.read: The anchor-tenant moment — though Microsoft signed ~$33B of neocloud deals in October 2025 alone (Nebius, Nscale, CoreWeave...), so Microsoft is diversifying across neoclouds while Lambda concentrates.

recentDevelopments.headline: Kansas City, MO AI factory: ~$500M conversion of a former Bank of America data-center campus — 24 MW and >10,000 Blackwell Ultra GPUs at early-2026 launch, scalable past 100 MW, dedicated to a single customer
recentDevelopments.read: Lambda's first owned-scale site — the beginning of a shift away from pure colocation, in a state paying data-center incentives.

recentDevelopments.headline: Reported: NVIDIA signs $1.5B four-year deal to lease ~18,000 of its own GPUs back from Lambda (~$1.3B for 10,000 GB300-class + ~$200M for 8,000 older chips) — making NVIDIA Lambda's largest customer per The Information
recentDevelopments.read: The sharpest instance of the sector's circular-financing pattern: the chip supplier is also an equity investor and now reportedly the biggest revenue line. Utilization is real but self-referential.

recentDevelopments.headline: Reported: Morgan Stanley, J.P. Morgan and Citi hired to prepare a U.S. IPO 'as soon as H1 2026' (The Information)
recentDevelopments.read: The IPO process began within months of CoreWeave's March 2025 listing validating neocloud multiples.

recentDevelopments.headline: Exited the on-prem hardware business (Vector workstations, Scalar/Hyperplane servers) after a decade; Inference API and Lambda Chat sunset weeks later
recentDevelopments.read: All side quests cut ahead of the S-1 — Lambda chose the capital-intensive contracted-cloud lane over its diversified developer heritage.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Lambda has executed a deliberate, near-total pivot from developer GPU cloud to contracted superintelligence infrastructure in preparation for a public listing. Basis: hardware business exited (Aug 2025), inference products sunset (Sep 2025), Microsoft and NVIDIA anchor contracts (Q4 2025), investor-relations and audit-chair appointments, and a professional CEO/CFO installed (2026) — every move since mid-2025 points the same direction.

(High confidence) We assess the NVIDIA relationship is simultaneously Lambda's moat and its largest structural risk. Basis: NVIDIA is chip supplier, Series D investor, and — per The Information — largest customer via the $1.5B leaseback; the August 2026 term loan finances an NVIDIA-tied chip purchase. The circular-financing critique applied to CoreWeave applies here with more force, because Lambda's concentration is undisclosed pending an S-1.

(Moderate confidence) We assess a 2026 IPO is contractually incentivized, not merely aspirational. Basis: the reported Mubadala convertible carries penalty terms if no listing within a year of January 2026; banks have been engaged since September 2025; timing has already slipped once (H1→H2 2026). Collection gap: no public S-1 exists as of 2026-08-21, and any filing would likely be confidential first.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the operational-quality gap versus CoreWeave is the valuation-relevant execution question. Basis: ClusterMAX held Lambda at Silver across 1.0 and 2.0 while Nebius/Crusoe/Fluidstack sit at Gold and CoreWeave alone at Platinum, citing capacity sell-outs and 'a general degree of disorganization'; Sacra pegs cloud gross margin ~61% vs CoreWeave's 74%. The Combes/Fisher/Hunter leadership import is the board's answer to exactly this.

(Moderate confidence) We assess capacity strategy is colocation-first with ownership just emerging, which caps near-term capex but also caps the power moat. Basis: EdgeConneX/Cologix/Prime/Aligned leases versus one owned conversion (Kansas City, ≤100 MW+ potential) against a stated 3 GW-by-2030 target. Collection gap: Lambda has never disclosed company-wide operating MW or GPU-fleet size — the widest disclosure gap among the major neoclouds.

financials.type: reported-private (no audited public statements; third-party figures attributed)

metrics.name: Revenue
metrics.actual: 2024 ~$425M (+~70%, Contrary Research); FY ended Sep 2025 >$520M with Q3 sales +80% YoY (The Information); ~$760M annualized exiting 2025 (Sacra estimate)
metrics.result: Cloud passed hardware in mid-2024; hardware exited Aug 2025 — the revenue base is now entirely cloud

metrics.name: Profitability
metrics.actual: ~$175M trailing-twelve-month net loss (The Information, Jan 2026); cloud gross margin ~61% vs CoreWeave ~74% (Sacra estimates)
metrics.result: Loss-making with thinner unit economics than the category leader

periods.commentary: Expectations honesty: Lambda publishes no financials and no analyst consensus exists — every figure here is The Information's reporting or Sacra/Contrary estimates, attributed as such. The S-1 will be the first audited look.

metrics.name: Priced equity rounds
metrics.actual: $1.5B (Series C $320M, Feb 2024) → ~$2.5B (Series D $480M, Feb 2025, NVIDIA/ARK/In-Q-Tel participating) → $5.9B post (Series E >$1.5B, Nov 2025, TWG Global lead — per Forge round data)
metrics.result: ~$2.36B total equity raised; Forge secondary at $39.32/share (2026-08-21) sits ~22% above the $32.27 Series E price

metrics.name: Debt ladder
metrics.actual: $500M Macquarie GPU-backed facility (Apr 2024, the sector's first) → $275M JPMorgan (Aug 2025) → $1B secured facility (May 2026, oversubscribed) → $926M TLB at Baa2/SOFR+300 (Aug 2026)
metrics.result: The first private neocloud with an investment-grade-rated term loan — the same coupon-compression arc CoreWeave traveled, compressed into two years

metrics.name: Pre-IPO convertible
metrics.actual: ≥$350M Mubadala-led notes (reported Jan 2026) priced ~20% below eventual IPO, penalties if no listing within a year
metrics.result: Reported H2 2026 listing window; Morgan Stanley/J.P. Morgan/Citi engaged since Sep 2025; no public S-1 as of 2026-08-21

periods.commentary: The capital structure tells the strategy: equity for land-grab speed, GPU-collateralized debt matched to contracted cash flows from a concentrated customer set (NVIDIA leaseback, Microsoft). Fully-amortizing structures mean the debt only works if the contracts pay to term.
